title: The Sacrifice of the New Creation - 6

content:
We come now to the last of the offerings in Numbers 15, and with it we bring to a close our long study of the sacrifice of the New Creation. After all the careful measurements of flour, oil, and wine, Yahweh gave one final instruction. He said that when Israel entered the land and ate its bread,
they were to take the first of their dough and present it to Yahweh as a heave offering. And there is something about this offering that immediately sets it apart from all the others in the chapter.

Every other offering in Numbers 15 was carefully measured. The flour was one-tenth, or two-tenths, or three-tenths of an ephah. The oil and wine were a fourth, a third, or a half of a hin. Everything was exact, everything was commanded to the precise amount. But this offering of the first of the dough had no measurement at all. Yahweh did not say how much. He simply said to bring the first of it. This is the one offering in the whole chapter with no fixed quantity, and that difference is not an accident. It teaches us a beautiful truth. The measured offerings teach us obedience to Yahweh's exact instruction.This unmeasured offering teaches us heart-level willingness within that obedience. Order and freedom are held together here, not set against each other. Yahweh is a God of order, and so most of the offering was measured precisely. But Yahweh is also a God who delights in a willing heart, and so this one offering was left open, that the worshipper might give freely from a glad and generous spirit. We are not to imagine that obedience and willingness are enemies. In Yahweh's worship they stand side by side. He commands the exact measure in some things, and He invites the free and willing gift in others.

The heart of this offering is the principle of firstfruits, which means giving Yahweh the first portion before we enjoy the rest ourselves. Israel was not to bake all their bread, eat their fill, and then, only if something happened to be left over, offer a little to God. They were to take the first of the dough and give it to Him before they ate. This principle reaches into every part of our lives.

It means giving Yahweh the first of the day, before the day is swallowed up by everything else. It means giving Him the first of our harvests, before it is all spent on ourselves. It means giving Him the first of our strength and our energy, and not merely the tired remainder at the end when we are too weary to serve. To bring the firstfruits is to say, "God, You come first, before I take anything for myself." It is the very opposite of giving God whatever happens to be left at the end.

But beneath this practical lesson lies a far deeper and more glorious truth, and it is fitting that we come to it as we close this whole study. The firstfruits point us to Christ. Paul writes, "And since Abraham and the other patriarchs were holy, their descendants will also be holy, just as the entire batch of dough is holy because the portion given as an offering is holy" (Romans 11:16). In the same way, Christ is the holy firstfruit, and all who are joined to Him are made holy through Him. The first portion sanctifies the whole lump. Because Christ, the firstfruit, is holy, all who belong to Him are counted holy in Him. And Paul teaches this same truth about the resurrection, saying, "But in fact, Christ has been raised from the dead. He is the first of a great harvest of all who have died" (1 Corinthians 15:20). He goes on to give the order, "But there is an order to this resurrection: Christ was raised as the first of the harvest; then all who belong to Christ will be raised when he comes back" (1 Corinthians 15:23). Christ is the firstfruit of the resurrection. Because He was raised, all who are His will surely be raised also. The first sheaf guarantees the whole harvest.

And the Scriptures show us something else that is very precious. Those who belong to Christ, the little flock, are themselves also called a kind of firstfruits. James writes, "He chose to give birth to us by giving us his true word. And we, out of all creation, became his prized possession"; his firstfruits (James 1:18). And in Revelation, the faithful who follow the Lamb are described as "a special offering to God and to the Lamb"; firstfruits unto God (Revelation 14:4). So the New Creation is not only sanctified by Christ the firstfruit, but is drawn into that same character, offered to God as a firstfruits, set apart and given wholly to Him. What a fitting truth on which to end our study of the sacrifice of the New Creation. We began with the lamb, the ram, and the young bull, and with the fine flour, the oil, and the wine that rose to meet them. We have seen that our character, our Spirit-filled life, and our poured-out devotion are acceptable only in Christ, and now we see that we ourselves are His firstfruits, holy because He is holy, and destined to share in His resurrection because He is the first of the harvest. So let us give God the first of everything through our Lord Jesus Christ, gladly and willingly, for Christ gave Himself first for us. He is the firstfruit that sanctifies us, the first of the harvest that assures us. And with this we close our study of the offerings, giving thanks to Yahweh for all that He has taught us through them.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,
We thank You for all You have taught us through these offerings of the New Creation.

Teach us to bring You the first of our days, our strength, and all we have, and not the leftover.

Join our obedience to Your exact command with the free and willing gladness of our hearts.

We thank You that Christ is the firstfruit who makes us holy, and the first of the harvest who assures our rising.

You have made us Your own firstfruits; let us be wholly and gladly given to You.

God chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits. James 1:18

In Christ name, the firstfruits from the dead, we pray. Amen.
